results.title: Price regulation in two-sided markets: Empirical evidence ...
results.content: # Price regulation in two-sided markets: Empirical evidence from debit cards. This paper provides empirical evidence of a well-known theoretical concern that market failures in two-sided markets are hard to identify and correct. We study the reactions of banks, merchants, and consumers to Dodd-Frank’s Durbin Amendment that lowered interchange fees on debit card transactions. Banks recouped a significant portion of their losses by charging consumers for products that they previously provided for free on the subsidized side of the two-sided market. :   We thank Toni Whited (Editor), Sumit Agarwal, Yakov Amihud, Jeremy Bulow, Sylvain Catherine, George Comer, Francesco D'Acunto, Itamar Dreschler, Erik Gilje, Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham (discussant), Paul Gompers, Sam Hanson, Andres Liberman (discussant), Jack Liebersohn (discussant), Scott Nelson, Pascal Noel, Dev Patel, Jonathan Roth, David Scharfstein, Andrei Shleifer, Philip Strahan (discussant), Larry Summers, Emily Williams, Susan Woodward (discussant), and seminar participants at the American Law and Economics Association, the Australasian Finance and Banking Conference, Berkeley Law, Boulder Summer Conference on Consumer Financial Decision Making, Erasmus University, George Mason, Georgetown University (McDonough), Harvard Business School, Maastricht University, Midwest Finance Association, NBER Summer Institute Household Finance Session, NYU Law and Finance Conference, Reserve Bank of Australia, Society for Empirical Legal Studies, Tilburg University, University of Virginia (Darden), WAPFIN, and Wharton for helpful comments.
